text:
For most UK sole traders and very small businesses, **Starling** is the strongest default, with **Mettle** close behind if free accounting software matters more than pure banking features.

There is no single best account. It depends on cash, accounting software, and whether you need a high-street branch.

### Quick picks

| Need | Best fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Most sole traders (digital payments) | **Starling** | Free, full bank, unlimited UK transfers, FSCS cover |
| Free bookkeeping / tax software | **Mettle** (NatWest) | Free account + FreeAgent included |
| Best app / already use Monzo | **Monzo Business Lite** | Strong service ratings; free tier |
| Built-in invoicing tools | **Tide** | Good tools; free plan has transfer limits |
| Lots of cash or branch access | **NatWest, HSBC, Barclays or Lloyds** | Counters and deposit machines |

### Starling (best overall for most people)
- **£0** monthly fee and **no charge** for UK Faster Payments, Direct Debits or standing orders.
- Fully licensed UK bank, so eligible deposits are **FSCS-protected** (limit is £120,000 per person per banking licence).
- Free links to accounting software (Xero, QuickBooks, FreeAgent) and built-in tools aimed at Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
- Cash can be paid in at the Post Office at **0.7% (minimum £3)**. Sole trader cash limits are tighter than for limited companies (around £5,000 a day and a lower annual cap — check the current figure before you rely on it).
- Weak spots: cash is relatively expensive if you bank a lot of it; overdrafts are not a given for sole traders.

### Mettle (best free package if you want FreeAgent)
- **£0** a month, free UK transfers, FSCS cover via NatWest.
- **FreeAgent included** (normally paid software) as long as you make at least one transaction a month. That can be worth well over £100 a year.
- Aimed at sole traders and very small companies (typically up to two owners).
- Limitations: no cheques, no international payments, and cash deposits cost more than Monzo’s.

### Monzo Business
- **Lite is free**, with free UK transfers and FSCS protection.
- Often ranks at or near the top of independent business banking service surveys, and the app is excellent.
- Cash deposits are relatively cheap (**£1 each** at Post Office / PayPoint), which helps trades and cash-heavy work.
- Accounting integrations and some tax features sit on the paid **Pro** plan (about £9 a month).

### Tide
Useful if you want invoicing, receipts and expense tools in the app. The free plan only includes a small number of free transfers (often five a month), then about **20p each**, so costs rise if you move money often. Current accounts are provided via ClearBank, so FSCS cover usually applies — confirm the latest terms.

### High-street banks
Worth it if you regularly pay in cash or want a counter:
- **NatWest**: startup/switch offers have included a period of free everyday banking, plus FreeAgent while you hold the account.
- **HSBC**: some small-business accounts have no monthly fee, with branch and Post Office access.
- **Barclays / Lloyds / Santander**: often free for an introductory period, then a monthly fee. Better for cash and in-branch service than the app-only banks.

### Practical points
- As a **sole trader** you are not legally required to have a business account, but most personal account terms ban business use, and a separate account makes tax and expenses much cleaner — especially with Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
- A **limited company** must keep company money separate from personal money.
- For sole traders, personal and business balances at the **same** bank are usually added together for the FSCS limit.
- E-money accounts (some Tide setups, ANNA, etc.) are safeguarded rather than always FSCS-protected in the same way as a bank. Prefer a licensed bank if protection matters to you.
- Fees, cash limits and free periods change. Check the provider’s current tariff before you apply, and look for any switch or signup bonus that is still live.

**Simple rule:** open **Starling** unless you specifically want FreeAgent free (**Mettle**), already live in the Monzo app (**Monzo Lite**), or bank a lot of cash in person (a high-street account).
